A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MrT5 research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagnostic simulations, continued pre-training, downstream task evaluations, runtime measurements, and gate-placement and per-sample analyses in Sections 4–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original experiments and additional outcomes for pooling baselines, TyDiQA-GoldP, and 1.23B-parameter models, including detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the stated P-controller with a PI controller incorporating smoothed proportional error and accumulated error, used throughout nondiagnostic MrT5 training. Appendix D adds an attention-score penalty to the previously two-term training loss. These substantially revise training, while retaining the single-layer gate and soft-training/hard-inference deletion mechanism.

E1.justification: v2 adds nine-language TyDiQA-GoldP question answering, including Bengali, Finnish, Indonesian, Korean, and Telugu beyond the earlier language coverage. It removes the English-only continued-pretraining and zero-shot span-corruption comparison. The 15-language multilingual training coverage, XNLI, diagnostic tasks, and two character-level tasks remain.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds adapted Boundary Predictor mean-pooling and Convolutional Pooling baselines to ByT5, random deletion, and fixed deletion. BP and CP also join the retained downstream comparisons in Tables 4–5. Conversely, the cited subword T5 scores in v1's character-task appendix tables disappear from the corresponding v2 tables; diagnostic T5 comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Diagnostics change from 31M-parameter models, 128-token sequences, and 20,000 steps to 15M models, 64-token sequences, and 30,000 steps. Continued pre-training increases from 3,000 to 5,000 steps and reports BPB instead of cross-entropy. Downstream budgets, learning-rate schedules, batches, and compression targets also change substantially. TyDiQA and large-model experiments introduce additional protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds an analysis of whether compression effectiveness and efficiency scale to 1.23B parameters. Figure 4 replaces separate fixed-alpha and P-controller gate-placement studies with a PI-controlled BPB/runtime analysis. The English-only versus multilingual transfer analysis is removed, while the per-sample deletion analysis is retained with revised models and findings.

E5.justification: Both versions report correlation coefficients and p-values in the per-sample plots and use Fisher's Z transformation to aggregate correlations. Neither reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, or run-to-run uncertainty for the principal performance results. Changed correlation and p-values do not constitute a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced under revised settings. All-language XNLI accuracy changes from ByT5/MrT5 51.34/49.63 to 64.72/65.31; Word Search changes from 75.37/74.30 to 76.61/72.02. These are not same-setting gains or losses. New results include MrT5's TyDiQA EM/F1 of 68.27/77.73 and large-model BPB of 0.74 versus ByT5's 0.70, alongside new baseline and per-language entries.

T1.justification: Formal changes concern the revised controller recurrence and the newly defined thresholded attention-score penalty; the baseline appendix also supplies boundary-pooling equations. The existing theoretical compute-saving assumptions and MAC derivation in Appendix C remain mathematically unchanged apart from notation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Although the central efficiency–performance contribution remains, the claimed multilingual contribution shifts from English-trained zero-shot transfer to language-specific compression learned through multilingual training. The introduction and conclusion extend claimed superiority from random/fixed deletion to pooling alternatives. The abstract also revises the maximum downstream sequence reduction from 80% to 75%.

C2.justification: v2 adds an attention-score inflation failure mechanism and its regularization rationale, interprets language-specific deletion through script information density, and explains larger-model efficiency through encoder depth. The earlier cross-script transfer interpretation disappears. Some new interpretation overreaches: Table 5 calls MrT5 most efficient across character tasks, although CP has greater spelling-correction runtime reduction, 23.13% versus 22.30%.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation: optional Gumbel noise, controller and attention-penalty parameters, attention-head and added-parameter counts, and detailed BP adaptations for padding, attention masks, and relative positions. It also documents validation sampling and large-model settings. However, Table 6's character-task training totals conflict with the prose identifying the final checkpoints. The code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially broaden positioning through discussion of neural tokenizers, MAGNET, MANTa, BLT, EvaByte, MambaByte, GemFilter, and earlier character models. Dynamic pooling moves beyond v1's characterization as usually involving supervision: v2 discusses its learned segmentation approach and implements an unsupervised adapted comparator.

P1.justification: The background and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. Section 5 changes from monolingual/multilingual comparisons to BPB–compression, runtime, and per-language analyses; downstream reporting is reorganized around four models. Appendices are restructured, with experimental details moving from B to E and separate method, baseline, and scaling sections added.

P2.justification: Table 2's three subtables become one grouped table, and downstream tables gain comparator columns and revised metric groupings. Figures 2–4 are redrawn with changed axes, legends, panel structures, and placement. v2 adds a 15-panel language figure and settings, large-model, and QA tables. The architecture diagram and theoretical compute curve are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important weakness in v1's comparative evidence by evaluating learned and convolutional pooling alternatives under shared setups. Multilingual QA and larger-model experiments substantially strengthen the evidence for applicability, while expanded training and baseline documentation improves reproducibility. Removing the monolingual transfer study narrows coverage, and the character-task efficiency overclaim and checkpoint inconsistency reduce precision. These drawbacks do not outweigh the substantially stronger evaluation of the central efficiency claim.
